title: Larry Poindexter, ‘Days of Our Lives’ & ‘S.W.A.T.’ Star, Killed in Pedestrian Accident – NBC News
body:
Veteran television actor Larry Poindexter, known for his recurring roles on “Days of Our Lives,” “General Hospital,” and the 2003 action film “S.W.A.T.,” died on Wednesday after succumbing to injuries sustained when a vehicle struck him while crossing a street in Los Angeles. The 63‑year‑old performer, whose career spanned more than three decades, was pronounced dead at a local hospital, bringing an abrupt end to a life marked by steady work in daytime drama and occasional forays into film.

Poindexter’s most recognizable television work came in the form of guest and supporting parts that helped shape the fabric of several long‑running soaps. He first appeared on “Days of Our Lives” in the early 1990s, portraying a charismatic lawyer who became entangled in the series’ hallmark love triangles and corporate intrigue. A few years later, he joined the cast of “General Hospital” as a charismatic physician, a role that earned him a modest fan following among the show’s dedicated viewership. Though never a household name, Poindexter’s reliable presence contributed to the continuity that daytime audiences rely on, especially during periods of cast turnover.

Beyond the small screen, Poindexter ventured into the world of feature films, most notably landing a supporting role in the high‑octane remake of “S.W.A.T.” starring Colin Farrell and Samuel L. Jackson. In the movie, he played a police liaison officer, a part that, while brief, showcased his ability to transition from melodramatic soap narratives to gritty action sequences. Industry insiders recall that his professionalism on set—arriving prepared, delivering lines with precision, and maintaining a collaborative spirit—made him a valued member of any ensemble, regardless of the project’s scale.

The circumstances of Poindexter’s death underscore ongoing concerns about pedestrian safety in urban environments. According to Los Angeles police, the accident occurred at a busy intersection during the early evening rush hour. Witnesses reported that the driver, whose identity has not yet been released, appeared to lose control of the vehicle while attempting to make a left turn, striking Poindexter as he crossed the crosswalk. The incident has reignited calls from local advocacy groups for improved crosswalk signaling and stricter enforcement of traffic laws, especially in areas with high foot traffic near entertainment districts.

Colleagues and fans have taken to social media to express their condolences, highlighting Poindexter’s generosity and mentorship to younger actors. “Larry was the kind of guy who made everyone feel welcome on set,” one former co‑star wrote. “He had a quiet confidence and a genuine love for the craft that inspired many of us.” Tributes also note his charitable work, including participation in annual fundraisers for children’s hospitals and involvement in community theater projects that aimed to bring the performing arts to underserved neighborhoods.

As the entertainment community mourns the loss of a steadfast performer, Poindexter’s body of work serves as a reminder of the essential roles that character actors play in sustaining long‑running series and enriching the storytelling landscape. While his name may not have topped billboards, his contributions helped maintain the continuity and emotional resonance that keep viewers returning day after day. The industry now looks to honor his memory by continuing the advocacy for safer streets that his untimely death has spotlighted, ensuring that future generations of actors and fans can navigate both the stage and the city with greater security.
